current_leader.name: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention engine
current_leader.state_transition: approved authorization -> capture/reversal still absent as network-specific deadline approaches -> combine PSP lifecycle state with merchant order/fulfillment state -> recommend CAPTURE/REVERSE/NO ACTION before integrity-fee trigger -> reconcile avoided scheme fee
current_leader.why_survived: Fresh attack evidence shows processor automation does not uniformly neutralize the wedge. Stripe offers automatic delayed capture shortly before authorization expiry, but it is opt-in and addresses missed capture rather than stale authorizations that should be reversed. Adyen commonly auto-expires major-network authorizations only after 28 days, while Mastercard final/undefined authorization integrity fees can trigger after seven days. Therefore eventual PSP expiry is not equivalent to pre-fee remediation.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: Mastercard final/undefined authorization integrity fees can trigger after seven days, while Adyen's common major-network auto-expiry is 28 days. Stripe automatic_delayed capture demonstrates first-party mitigation for missed capture, but does not solve the cross-system decision to reverse an order that will not fulfill. Braintree's Visa guidance explicitly tells merchants to reverse/cancel quickly to minimize integrity fees.
current_leader.closest_threat: PSP-native automatic capture/expiry, gateway capture settings, and broad payment-operations products. Stripe's automatic delayed capture is the strongest first-party threat found this run, but it is not an exact reversal/capture decision layer across PSPs and merchant fulfillment systems.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read authorization, capture, cancel/reversal webhooks plus order/fulfillment state. Maintain network/MCC/region deadline table. Before the earliest applicable fee deadline output CAPTURE NOW, REVERSE NOW, or NO ACTION with projected fee. Leave execution merchant-confirmed or use the merchant's existing PSP API under explicit authorization.
current_leader.monetization: Per prevented-fee event or capped percentage of verified integrity fees avoided, aggregated monthly; use a low monitoring minimum only where expected avoided fees exceed the charge.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Actual merchant incidence is still unquantified. If stale authorizations are rare outside a small set of verticals, the recoverable fee pool may be too small even though the mechanism is technically clean. Exact enterprise payment-operations products may also handle this control without marketing it separately.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify incidence and dollars per 100k authorizations using processor/acquirer fee statements or public merchant data; identify verticals with manual/delayed capture and cancellation-heavy fulfillment; search payment-operations platforms for explicit automatic stale-authorization reversal before Visa/Mastercard integrity deadlines. Gate 6/8 only pass if the avoided-fee pool is material and exact incumbent coverage remains absent.

New rule: distinguish CAPTURE automation from REVERSE automation; one does not necessarily neutralize the other.
